core.generalErrorMessage: Something went wrong, please check the configuration
core.title: Core Settings
coreEditor.saveHint: Changes stay here until you press Save. Before saving, Xray itself checks the whole config; a config it can't load is refused and nothing changes.
coreEditor.certHint: Paths on the panel server; nodes get the files' content from the panel.
coreEditor.realityDestHint: A real TLS 1.3 site and port that REALITY imitates, e.g. www.microsoft.com:443
coreEditor.shortIdsHint: Hex, even length, at most 16 characters; separate with commas.
coreEditor.sniffingHint: Needed for routing by domain and for the http/tls/quic protocol rules.
coreEditor.renameHint: A renamed inbound is a new inbound to Marzban: hosts, node selections and user settings stay with the old tag. Routing rules are updated.
coreEditor.inboundsHint: Marzban adds every user to these inbounds. An inbound runs on the nodes that have it ticked; nodes that run every inbound get new ones automatically.
coreEditor.inboundFromLinkHint: Paste one vless://, vmess://, trojan:// or ss:// link: protocol, port, transport and security are copied. A REALITY inbound gets a new key pair of its own.
coreEditor.outboundsHint: Traffic leaves through these. The first one is the default for traffic that no routing rule catches.
coreEditor.importLinksHint: One link per line (vless://, vmess://, trojan://, ss://). Each becomes an outbound named after the link's remark.
coreEditor.fillFromLink: Paste a link to fill this form
coreEditor.routingHint: Rules are checked from the top; the first match decides the outbound.
coreEditor.noRules: No rules: all traffic goes to the first outbound.
coreEditor.preset.directIran: Iranian sites and IPs go direct
coreEditor.balancersInJson: {{count}} balancer(s): edit them in the JSON tab
coreEditor.ruleInboundsHint: None ticked: traffic of every inbound.
coreEditor.ruleDomainsHint: One per line: example.com, domain:, full:, keyword:, regexp:, geosite:
coreEditor.ruleIpsHint: One per line: IP, CIDR or geoip:
coreEditor.ruleUsersHint: Marzban's user emails look like ID.username, e.g. 12.ali
coreEditor.errors.formCantShow: The form can't show this; keep editing it as JSON
coreEditor.errors.badLink: This link is incomplete or broken
coreEditor.errors.unsupportedLink: Only vless://, vmess://, trojan:// and ss:// links are supported
coreEditor.errors.unsupportedTransport: This transport isn't supported (use tcp, ws, grpc, httpupgrade, xhttp or kcp)
coreEditor.errors.realityNeedsPublicKey: A REALITY link needs its public key (pbk)
coreEditor.errors.tagComma: A tag can't contain a comma
coreEditor.errors.certificate: TLS needs a certificate file and a key file
coreEditor.errors.realityServerNames: REALITY needs at least one server name
coreEditor.errors.realityPrivateKey: REALITY needs a private key: press Generate keys
coreEditor.errors.realityShortIds: Short IDs must be hex with an even length (at most 16)
coreEditor.errors.realityPublicKey: REALITY needs the server's public key
coreEditor.errors.wireguardKeys: WireGuard needs the secret key and the peer public key
coreEditor.errors.wireguardAddress: WireGuard needs at least one local address
coreEditor.errors.outboundInUse: {{count}} routing rule(s) use this outbound: change them first
coreEditor.errors.lastOutbound: Xray needs at least one outbound
coreEditor.errors.ruleCondition: Fill in at least one condition

hostsDialog.dataLimit: The usage limit of the user
hostsDialog.dataUsage: The current usage of the user
hostsDialog.desc: Use these variables to make it dynamic
hostsDialog.fragment.info.attention: Attention: currently, this feature only supported in streisand >= 1.6.12 and v2rayNG >= 1.8.16 (custom config)
hostsDialog.noise.info.attention: Attention: currently, this feature only supported in streisand >= 1.6.32 and v2rayNG >= 1.8.39 (custom config)
hostsDialog.host.info: By default, if a request host is set in the Xray config, this host is used. However, you can set a custom request host here if needed.
hostsDialog.host.multiHost: To set multiple addresses, separate them with <badge>,</badge> Each time an address is chosen randomly.
hostsDialog.host.wildcard: Use <badge>*</badge> to generate a random string (works for wildcard domain names)
hostsDialog.jalaliExpireDate: Expiry date of the user in solar calendar
hostsDialog.path.info: Set a path for host users, useful behind a reverse proxy.
hostsDialog.port.info: By default, a host uses the default port of the inbound. You can set a custom port in case this host is a server that forwards traffic from a port that differs from your server's port. For example, the server may forward traffic from port 8443 to the default port of your inbound server.
hostsDialog.proxyOutbound.info: Extra outbound ( only in v2ray custom config )
hostsDialog.security.info: If the middleware server of this host uses a different security layer than the inbound's default, you can set a custom security layer here.
hostsDialog.sni.info: By default, a host uses the default SNI of the inbound. You can set a custom SNI in case this host is a server that has a different SNI. For example, the server may receive traffic with a different SSL certificate, perform SSL termination, and forward it to your inbound server.
hostsDialog.title: Using this setting, you are able to assign specific address for each inbound.
login.welcomeBack: Welcome back, please enter your details
nodes.addHostForEveryInbound: Add this node as a new host for every inbound it runs
nodes.allowedInboundsHint: Only checked inbounds are built on this node. The panel server itself runs no inbounds: a config works only through a connected node that runs it. To serve configs on the panel server, run a node on it (local-node.sh) with address 127.0.0.1.
nodes.allowedInboundsHintAuto: Only checked inbounds are built on this node, and they stop running on the main server. With every box checked the node runs all inbounds and the main server keeps them too.
nodes.connection-hint: To setup a Marzban Node, you need to set this certificate on the node to initialize a secure connection between main server and the node
nodes.title: Using Marzban-Node, you are able to scale up your connection quality by adding different nodes on different servers.
